newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower, supply concerns looms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower, supply concerns looms.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished slightly lower, as supply concerns loomed over the market despite data confirming a slowdown in U.S. economic activity, traders and analysts said.
U.S. Treasury will sell $10.0 billion 10-year notes Wednesday and auction $10.0 billion 30-year T-bonds Thursday.
Treasury will begin auctioning Tuesday with the sale of $18.5 billion three-year notes.
"It's really amazing the Treasury will be auctioning three-years (notes) on election day," one floor trader said.
While a Reuters poll showed that President Clinton's lead against Republican challenger Bob Dole narrowed, traders said the market was focused on the Congressional races.

They said fears about a Democratic sweep in Congress were undermining the market, and that an upset in the Republican-controlled legislature could exacerbate pressures if the three-year note aution is poorly absorbed.
"The street may just stay out of the way," he said.
Funds were good sellers in the Eurodollar market, helping to push out the December-March spread. Earlier in the session, the spread inverted, as March traded up to 94.51.

"Before September, you couldn't find anyone holding paper out more than a year," he said. "But then everyone ran into two-years (notes), and now you are seeing money being put to work in seven years."

Traders said order flow was light in Eurodollars as "the market basically got what they wanted," one trader said. Payrolls and the unemployment rate were as expected, while average hourly earnings were unchanged.
October National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) dropped below the average trade forecast, as well, and helped boost December T-bonds USZ6 toward 113-28/32.
However, the momentum was too weak to lift December to the daily high, and the contract soon found offers.
"You'd have to be disconcerted that we saw positive data and the market was pretty much flat," said James Florsheim, senior vice president at Chicago Corp.
A trader said one firm bought 20,000 five- and 10-year note puts this week, which also weighed on the market.

At the end of pit trade, December bonds fell 08/32 at 112-24/32, 10-year notes were down 03/32 at 109-17/32, March Eurodollars were off two basis points at 94.42, and June Eurodollars were down two basis poinst at 94.31.
